clue.text: Help as Brie deteriorates — being this?

definitions.text: Help as Brie deteriorates — being this?

indicators.note: a cheese that deteriorates breaks down, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A worried cheese-lover watches a Brie go off and wonders what kind of food it must be.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: shuffle the letters of 'Help as Brie' and you get a word for food that goes off, which is exactly what a deteriorating Brie is.
explanation.definitionFit: Food liable to rot or spoil quickly is described as perishable, and soft cheese is a classic example.

clue.text: Area within location for splendid residence

indicators.note: Area sits within the word for location, so its letter goes inside

parts.note: a location is a place

explanation.surface: An estate agent's blurb: a fine house in a great spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A palace is a grand official home of a monarch or bishop, the very model of a splendid residence.

clue.text: Macaque needs bringing back to life outside hospital

indicators.note: the reviving word goes outside the hospital letter, wrapping round it

parts.note: resus is the medical shorthand for resuscitation, reviving a patient
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A monkey near death needs reviving, though not in a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like it means 'not in hospital', but it tells you to put RESUS around H.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus monkey is a species of macaque, much used in medical research.

clue.text: Miss out on prince's appearance?

parts.note: read as a young lady ('Miss') who is out cold until her prince turns up to wake her, the fairy-tale princess

explanation.surface: Someone fails to see a royal visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss out on' reads as failing to see; instead 'Miss' is a girl and 'out' means unconscious, a state that lasts until the prince appears.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale, a cursed princess sleeps for a hundred years until a prince's kiss wakes her.

clue.text: Three-wheeler following parades hit from above

indicators.note: the vehicle comes after the parades word, so it is placed second

parts.note: to parade opinions is to air them, so parades gives airs
a trike is a tricycle, a three-wheeled vehicle

explanation.surface: A tricycle trailing a procession gets struck from overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: A military attack by aircraft bombing or firing on a target below is an air strike.

clue.text: Spear in butcher's no good

indicators.note: no good says the letter for good is left out of the look word

parts.note: rhyming slang: butcher's hook means look, so a butcher's is a glance

explanation.surface: A spear in a butcher's shop is useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butcher's' is British rhyming slang (butcher's hook = look): 'have a butcher's' means take a look. Removing G from GLANCE leaves the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A lance is a long spear carried by a mounted knight.

clue.text: Owed pound in honourable affair

parts.note: money owed is due
L stands for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A debt of a pound is owed in a matter of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A duel was a formal fight between gentlemen to settle a point of honour.

clue.text: Marriage is with Democrat in the end, not Republican

parts.note: a marriage is a union

indicators.note: points to the end of the word Democrat, its final letter

explanation.surface: American politics: a wedding where a Democrat wins out over a Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is American; the definition is from Northern Ireland, where unionists, who want to stay in the UK, oppose republicans, who want a united Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In Northern Irish politics, supporters of the union with Britain stand opposite republicans.

clue.text: Letter also featured in amusing write-up?

indicators.note: the word for also is featured in the middle of the other piece
in a down clue a write-up is read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: something amusing is droll
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A letter appearing in a comic review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not a written character but one who lets property; 'write-up' in a down clue means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lets out a property to tenants is literally a letter, a crossword-only sense.

clue.text: Somewhat limited success as year in Down ends badly

indicators.note: the words are arranged badly, so they must be shuffled into the right order

explanation.surface: A short-lived triumph, as the year in County Down finishes poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is only a link. Down is a county in Northern Ireland, but here it is just anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nine days' wonder is a sensation that excites interest briefly and is soon forgotten.

clue.text: Pork pie and case of Grenache for lord

parts.note: rhyming slang: a porky pie, or pork pie, is a lie

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nobleman's picnic of pork pie and a bottle of red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' is British rhyming slang for lie (usually shortened to 'porky'); Grenache is a red wine grape.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a feudal superior to whom vassals owe allegiance, a lord.

clue.text: Start to read publication that includes new version

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
the publication word includes the letter for new inside it

parts.note: an edition is one issue of a publication

explanation.surface: Begin reading a magazine that carries a revised text.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation, one particular version of a piece.

clue.text: Savoury cake politician dipped in salt pot

indicators.note: the politician is dipped into the pot, so goes inside it

parts.note: a cruet is a small container for salt or other condiments
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician's snack plunged into the salt cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumpet is a soft griddle cake, toasted and eaten buttered, so savoury rather than sweet.

clue.text: Deathless seabird observed in wild lea

indicators.note: the seabird sits in the shuffled meadow word
the meadow word is wild, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An immortal bird spotted on an untamed meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lea' is a poetic word for a meadow, here only fodder for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: What is eternal lasts for ever, and so is never subject to death.

clue.text: Chair covering — not for mum? — Charlie carried in vehicle

parts.note: being against something is not for it, anti
ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: the fool is carried inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a charlie is British slang for a fool, an ass

explanation.surface: A chair cover that mother dislikes, with a man named Charlie riding in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like C from the NATO alphabet, but here it is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: An antimacassar is a cloth laid over a chair back to protect it from hair oil.

clue.text: Great soldier brings cross into a famous rowing club

indicators.note: the cross goes into the middle of the other letters

parts.note: Leander Club at Henley-on-Thames is one of the oldest rowing clubs
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A war hero brings a crucifix to a celebrated boat club.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander is an English rowing club at Henley, home of the Henley regatta.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great conquered an empire from Greece to India and is among history's greatest generals.

clue.text: Heavenly grub in bar: I am so excited!

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled at finding divine food in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambrosia was the food of the Greek gods, granting immortality.

clue.text: Support ecstasy habit, immoral, keeping place for it?

parts.note: E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: the immoral habit word keeps the place inside it

parts.note: an immoral habit is a vice
a den, as in den of iniquity, is a place where vice goes on

explanation.surface: Funding someone's drug habit, with a spot set aside for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is material that supports or backs up a claim, as in 'the data support it'.

clue.text: For example Pancake Day hamper?

definitions.meaning: a festival whose date shifts each year with Easter, like Shrove Tuesday
a picnic hamper is, whimsically, a banquet you can carry about

explanation.walkthrough: Pancake Day is the British name for Shrove Tuesday, which falls on a different date each year.
explanation.definitionFit: A church festival with no fixed date is called this, and a portable picnic basket is literally one too.

clue.text: Cake and a drink in heart of Burgundy

indicators.note: the drink goes inside the middle letters
the heart of a word is its middle letters

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Dessert and a drink in central Burgundy.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgundy is both a wine and a French region, but here it only supplies its two central letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich cream cake, the French word for cake.

clue.text: Euros revolutionary: regard finally shown for 'woke'

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged
finally takes the final letter of regard

explanation.surface: Political chatter: Eurosceptic radicals finally paying regard to 'woke' views.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woke' looks political but here means simply awoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean stirred from sleep: someone who woke was roused.

clue.text: Beaming princess almost taken in by traitor

indicators.note: the princess is taken inside the traitor word

parts.note: a rat is someone who betrays others

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A smiling princess is nearly fooled by a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: The princess is Diana, Princess of Wales, the best-known princess in British crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiant face glows with happiness, just as a beaming one does.

clue.text: Inventor renovates large houses

indicators.note: the words house the letters, holding them inside

explanation.surface: An inventor does up big homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'houses' looks like a noun but is the verb: the letters sit inside 'renovates large'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was the Serbian-American inventor of alternating-current systems.

clue.text: Fuss about vocab omitting British fruit

indicators.note: the fuss word goes about the other letters, around them

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

indicators.note: the letter for British is left out

explanation.surface: A row over vocabulary that leaves out British words, with fruit thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means around here, not concerning: the fuss word wraps the shortened vocabulary word.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is a pear-shaped fruit with a large stone.

clue.text: Ground is stained, so decontaminated

indicators.note: ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A floor is marked, so it was cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like the noun, floor; it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sanitised has been cleaned of germs, made hygienic and free of contamination.

clue.text: 500 on steamship wear formal clothes

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
re means on or about, as in a memo

explanation.surface: Five hundred passengers on a liner put on evening wear.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress, as for dinner, is to put on formal attire.

clue.text: Swear as dance party beginning to end?

indicators.note: the first letter moves from the beginning to the end

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: Swearing as a party goes from start to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to end' looks like 'all night long' but tells you to move R from the front of RAVE to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to state firmly or assert, as one does when swearing to something.

clue.text: Entertainment centre just by stadium

parts.note: something just is fair
a sports stadium is a ground

explanation.surface: An amusements venue next to a sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground is an open site with rides and stalls for amusement.
